title: Abstracts 3
program_note:
Abstracts 3 is, in part, an arrangement for trio of some of the movements of Abstracts 2, with additional original music. It was inspired by manhole covers in city streets (mostly in Moscow), some abstractly, some more directly pictorially. “Labyrinthe” reminded me of the labyrinth of Chartres Cathedral, and its timeless spirituality. “Neural Net” made me think of a network of multiple linear connections.  In “Twelve-Bar Benzenes,” the arrangement of hexagons — benzene rings? — in circles of twelve brought to mind both the harmonic cycles of the Blues and of other numerically-regular cycles of phrases and pitches.  “Gothic Arches” made me think first of the soaring arches of Notre Dame Cathedral and other French cathedrals, but then of the idea of melodic lines soaring into heaven and falling into the depths.

Abstracts 3 is about 14’40” total duration, with the individual movements approximately as shown:
1.  Labyrinthe (2’30”)
2.  Neural Net (clarinet solo) (2’50”)
iii. Twelve-Bar Benzenes (’cello solo) (3’35”) (attacca)
1.  Gothic Arches (5’45”)

David S. Lefkowitz
Los Angeles, CA
15 March, 2019
